name: gobo
desc: Free and portable Eiffel tools and libraries
why: Eiffel tools and libraries bring Design by Contract to the terminal, an unusual language ecosystem most developers never touch.

brief.what_it_is: Gobo Eiffel is an open-source collection of compilers, tools and libraries for the Eiffel programming language, distributed as a downloadable archive or source tarball. The README lists 19 Eiffel libraries (kernel, lexical, parse, regexp, XML, XPath, XSLT, test, thread, time and others) and 13 command-line utilities: geant, gec, gecc, gecop, gedoc, geimage, gelsp, gelex, gelint, gepp, getest, gexslt and geyacc. The utilities are optional, since the library classes can be used on their own. The README says the tools are built to run across different Eiffel compilers, and it lists gec (the Gobo Eiffel Compiler) and ISE Eiffel as supported compilers.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says one of the project's main concerns is to give the Eiffel community tools and libraries that are free and portable across Eiffel compilers, so developers can keep using their favourite compiler and still get the Gobo extras.
brief.how_it_works: The utilities are written in Eiffel and built from source with a script, using either the bundled Zig toolchain or a system C compiler as the backend. Installation means unpacking a release, pointing the GOBO environment variable at it, adding its bin directory to PATH, and running install.sh. The README also notes that Eiffel compilers use $NAME for environment variables in their ECF files, so the project uses that convention rather than Windows %NAME%.

commands_seen.context: Builds the Gobo tools such as gec and geyacc. The argument is zig if the Zig toolchain was installed, or a system C compiler such as gcc.
Optional step after copying a Zig download into the tool directory, to patch it for use with the Gobo build. The README gives it with no further explanation.

brief.install_notes: Download the release archive for your platform and architecture (Windows: gobo-windows-{x86_64,arm64}-*.7z; Linux: gobo-linux-*.tar.xz; macOS: gobo-macos-*.tar.xz; other platforms: the gobo-*.tar.gz source package or a Git checkout). Unpack it to a directory of your choice, optionally set GOBO (Windows: %GOBO%) to that directory, and add its bin directory to PATH. For the tools, run bin/install.sh with a C compiler, or install Zig first. Zig is optional: download it, place it in tool/gec/backend/c/zig with the zig executable at the root, and run the patch script. The README also points to ISE Eiffel as a supported compiler, but no ISE-specific steps are listed.
brief.standout: Most Eiffel tooling is tied to one vendor's compiler. Gobo is designed to work across several Eiffel compilers and ships its own compiler (gec) with a bundled Zig-based C backend. The project covers a whole toolchain (lexer and parser generators, linter, preprocessor, test runner, XSLT processor, language server) under the MIT license. The scout note's pitch of bringing Design by Contract to the terminal is not the README's own framing; the README describes compilers and tools for Eiffel, and the homepage mentions Design by Contract in the context of consulting.
brief.status: Maintained. The README lists gec 26.10.18 as a supported compiler version, the copyright line runs to 2026, and it advertises a nightly build with features under development. The repository has about 9,458 commits, 64 stars and 26 forks. I did not see a last-commit date on the page, so this rests on the version and copyright evidence.
brief.caveats: The README says the software has only been tested on Windows 11, Ubuntu Linux and macOS, and that other Eiffel compilers and versions have not been tested. Building the tools needs a C compiler or the optional Zig download, so setup is not a single brew install. The Zig patch step is given with no explanation. The utilities are only useful if you need them; the libraries can be used alone. The homepage fetched was the consulting company's page (Gobosoft, a services business run by the project's creator) and not a product page, so the open-source details come from the GitHub README.
quotes: One of the main concerns of the Gobo Eiffel Project is to provide the Eiffel community with Eiffel tools and libraries that are free and portable across various Eiffel compilers available on the market.
The software included in this package is copyrighted freeware distributed under the terms and conditions of the MIT License as specified in License file.
Note that these utilities are not needed if you just want to use the library classes provided in this package.
